# Onboarding and learner overview

`ms-go-student` owns one versioned onboarding profile per student. The student
declares a direction, self-assessed experience, known and desired stacks, goal,
preferred language, weekly time budget, and pace through:

- `GET /api/v1/student/onboarding`;
- `PUT /api/v1/student/onboarding` with `expected_version` (`0` creates the
  first version).

The actor comes only from the trusted gateway headers. A stale version returns
`409`. Values are normalized and bounded before persistence.

Self-assessed experience and known stacks are initial hypotheses. They never
create mastery evidence, change `student_target_mastery`, or replace future
placement diagnostics.

## Atomic Teacher onboarding turn v2

The additive internal turn contract is separate from public onboarding. Only
Teacher may call the dedicated-token endpoints:

- `POST /internal/v1/teacher/students/{studentID}/onboarding/turns` accepts
  `student-onboarding-turn.v2` and returns
  `student-onboarding-turn-result.v2`.
- `GET /internal/v1/teacher/students/{studentID}/onboarding/turns/{studentCommandID}`
  returns the narrow immutable recovery receipt.
- `POST /internal/v1/teacher/students/{studentID}/onboarding/turns/{studentCommandID}/prove-no-effect`
  accepts `student-onboarding-turn-no-effect-proof.v2`.

The URL supplies the student identity. Apply requires `Idempotency-Key` equal
to `student_command_id`; prove requires the URL, header, and embedded command
IDs to agree. Bodies are strict, capped at 16 KiB, and reject raw model output,
message bodies, assistant UI payloads, arbitrary metadata, and profile-shaped
writes.

Student validates the bounded typed-slot command, normalizes its UUID and
onboarding values, and atomically records one immutable accepted draft/profile
effect with provenance, or one immutable `no_effect` recovery receipt. Absence
from GET is never proof that no effect occurred. `explicit_ui` and
`explicit_text` are the only accepted origins in this slice; inferred and
default values are reserved.

`TEACHER_ONBOARDING_TURN_V2_ENABLED` defaults to `false`. A new apply then
returns `503` without writing an effect, while exact replay, GET recovery, and
prove-no-effect remain available. This slice does not call Dialog, AI Prompt,
or Planner and does not start S6-or-later orchestration.

## General teacher projection

`GET /internal/students/{studentID}/learner-overview` requires the exact shared
internal token. It returns:

- the optional onboarding profile;
- at most 20 current target-mastery rows ordered by most recent evidence;
- the current learning path, bounded to 50 ordered items;
- the latest diagnostic snapshot, bounded to 100 targets;
- the five most recent learning-session summaries.

It returns no answer identity, official action outcome, raw evidence, reducer
audit, dialog history, prompt data, or inferred diagnosis. A student without an
onboarding profile still has a valid empty/bounded overview, allowing the
teacher to explain that personalization data is not yet available instead of
inventing it. The projection is `student-learner-overview-v2`; consumers fail
closed on other versions.

## Planner readiness projection

`GET /internal/students/{studentID}/planning-readiness` is a separate,
read-only `student-planning-readiness-snapshot.v1` contract for Learning
Planner. It is protected by the exact shared internal token and reads the
current state in one PostgreSQL repeatable-read, read-only transaction.

An active accepted draft (`version >= 1`) has deterministic precedence over a
finalized profile so an unfinished beginner profile remains factual rather than
being filled with defaults. `state_ref` is `{kind, version}` where kind is
`none`, `accepted_draft`, or `finalized_profile`; only `none` has version zero.
Both stack fields are `{state, values?}`: `answered` can carry a concrete empty
array, `unanswered` means no draft answer, and `unresolved` avoids claiming an
explicit empty legacy-profile value that existing storage cannot prove.
For `desired_stacks`, the existing write contract rejects an answered-empty
draft; an authoritative no-selection readiness snapshot is therefore
`{"state":"unanswered"}`. The read projection does not loosen S3 writes.

`learning_intent` is emitted only when the authoritative `goal_code` is exactly
`learn_programming`; its source is always `onboarding_goal_code.v1`. No
direction or fuzzy mapping produces an intent. Preferred-language evidence is
trusted only when matching accepted `explicit_ui` or `explicit_text` turn
provenance exists. An unprovenanced stored language is marked
`untrusted_persisted`, and `content_language` is omitted for it. When present,
`content_language` has `source: preferred_language` and the same trusted code
and provenance. Finalization preserves earlier explicit language evidence only
when the completed draft points to that exact profile version and the latest
matching provenance belongs to the completed draft's accepted version lineage;
legacy rows without that proof remain untrusted.

`active_path` is observational, never a Planner command: it appears only for
the exact selected `ACTIVE` Student path and contains its path id, version,
Course id, goal, and literal `ACTIVE` status. The response
does not write onboarding state, alter Course/path state, create an outbox row,
or accept a request body/idempotency key.

## Learning journey

Student owns the current path and its immutable version audit. Learning Planner
may replace it only through its dedicated-token
`PUT /internal/students/{studentID}/learning-path` command with an optimistic
`expected_version`, canonical Course fingerprint/revision, and explicit Planner
policy metadata. Teacher has no write access. Each item is a Course lesson
reference with current Student-owned status; no Course content or target graph
is copied here. Path responses expose `course_fingerprint`; the existing
`curriculum_revision` field remains an equal compatibility alias during client
migration.

When a replan finds no remaining gap for the same goal, Learning Planner calls
`PUT /internal/students/{studentID}/learning-path/completion`. Student verifies
the expected version, goal, and Course fingerprint, preserves already completed
items, marks other items `SKIPPED_MASTERED`, and stores one audited revision.
Repeating an already applied completion is a no-op. A path for another goal or
fingerprint returns a conflict.

`POST /internal/students/{studentID}/diagnostics/snapshots` captures the current
mastery distribution for an exact bounded target set. Missing evidence remains
explicitly `UNKNOWN`; declared onboarding experience never becomes diagnostic
evidence.

Students start and end one active `LearningSession` through
`/api/v1/student/learning-sessions`. Start accepts an optional
`analytics_session_id` UUID so raw Statistic activity can be correlated without
making analytics the session owner. Trusted processors may attach bounded
active-learning counters through
`PUT /internal/students/{studentID}/learning-sessions/{sessionID}/metrics` using
optimistic versioning. The exact session is available to trusted orchestration
through `GET /internal/students/{studentID}/learning-sessions/{sessionID}`.
Stored counters cover lessons, tasks, questions, selected explanations, code
runs, failures, passed tests, hints, interventions, and stuck signals.
Wall-clock duration is not treated as active learning.
